hints.S05_A1: The dash explains it: every STALL busy, every SEAT filled, and the place is compared to an ANT COLONY. Ask: does an ant colony sit still and silent, or hum with movement and sound? Match the word to that hum.
hints.S05_A2: The clue is 'in ONE SMOOTH MOVEMENT' onto the PLATE. Ask: how do you move rice with a spoon or ladle - by pouring liquid, by throwing, by cutting, or by lifting it up in one curved motion?
hints.S05_A3: He gives regular CUSTOMERS EXTRA CHILLI and SAUCE, so he is putting more in, not taking anything away. Ask: which phrase means to include something extra? The others mean escaping, quitting, or forcing your way in.
hints.S05_A4: It was the MOST DELICIOUS thing Sam had ever EATEN - so how must he feel? Ask: does this idiom describe great delight, or illness, or trouble, or confusion? An idiom cannot be read word by word.
hints.S05_A5: A burst of STEAM rose the instant the vegetables hit the hot WOK - they went in fast, not gently. Ask: which verb means to throw something quickly into a pan? 'Placed' is slow and careful, and 'carried' puts nothing in.
hints.S05_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not 'the CLASS'. Words like nobody and everybody behave like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb or the verb with -s? This is a fact, not an action in progress.
hints.S05_B2: 'Only a LITTLE BIT of CURRY' - how many things are you counting? Ask: does the amount left in the POT count as one single thing, or as many things? Match the verb to that amount, and remember the curry has not been eaten yet, so do not reach for a past form.
hints.S05_B3: The waiter SUDDENLY DROPPED the tray right in the middle of your meal. Ask: which choice shows an action already going on in the past when something else cut across it? A plain past verb only shows a finished action.
hints.S05_B4: THAN tells you two things are being compared, and 'delicious' is a long adjective. Ask: do long adjectives take -er, or do they need a helper word in front? The -est form is for three or several, and 'deliciouser' is not English.
hints.S05_B5: The word YET at the end, together with TRIED (a past participle), tells you the question is about any time up to now. Ask: which helping verb goes with a past participle to make the present perfect? 'Did' would need the plain verb 'try'.
hints.S05_B6: A tag mirrors the statement's verb: the sentence uses IS ('The hawker centre IS one of...'). Ask: after a positive statement, must the tag turn negative or stay positive? And should the tag keep the same verb rather than borrow 'do'?
hints.S05_B7: GLASS begins with the consonant sound /g/, and the auntie is not pointing to one particular glass the reader already knows. Ask: which article goes before consonant sounds, and which goes before vowel sounds?
hints.S05_B8: The two halves of the sentence pull against each other: the food was SPICY, yet the children ate it HAPPILY. Ask: which joining word signals a contrast or surprise? 'Because' gives a reason, and 'so' gives a result.
hints.S05_C1: The writer says MY FAMILY loves going there - the house belongs to the writer together with the family. Ask: which possessive word means 'belonging to me and the people I live with'? Not one person alone, and not somebody else's.
hints.S05_C2: These words are inside the SISTER's speech, and she is pointing at the CHICKEN RICE STALL - the food belongs to the people who run that stall. Ask: which possessive word points to other people, not to you?
hints.S05_C3: Father comes back with FIVE PLATES and puts those plates down on the table. Ask: which pronoun stands for more than one thing that is being acted upon? The plates are objects, and there are several.
hints.S05_C4: The uncle SAW the whole family sitting TOGETHER - and the writer is part of that family, seen from outside. Ask: which pronoun means 'me and the people with me' when we are the ones being looked at, not the ones doing the looking?
hints.S05_C5: He is speaking about the small BOWL of SOUP he has just brought over. Ask: which pronoun stands for a single thing that is neither male nor female? The blank starts the sentence, so you need the subject form.
hints.S05_C6: Mother THANKED the chicken rice UNCLE - one man, and he is the person receiving her thanks. Ask: which pronoun replaces a single male in the object position? Not the possessive, and not the subject form 'he'.
hints.S05_C7: 'A rich FLAVOUR all of ___ OWN' - the flavour belongs to the SOUP, and soup is a thing, not a person. Ask: which possessive word belongs to a thing? Careful: the look-alike with an apostrophe is short for 'it is'.
hints.S05_C8: The SISTER hugs the MOTHER, and that mother belongs to the sister - one girl. Ask: which possessive word shows something belonging to a single female? Match the pronoun to who the mother belongs to.
hints.S05_D1: Your NOSE notices it first: FRIED GARLIC and GRILLED FISH, floating through the whole market. Ask: which box word names something you take in through your nose? The blank follows 'The', so it must be a noun.
hints.S05_D2: Many people are STANDING in a LONG line at the POPULAR fish stall. Ask: which box word names a line of people waiting for their turn? The blank comes after 'a long', so it has to be a noun.
hints.S05_D3: The blank sits between 'We' and PATIENTLY, so it is a verb - and the story happened LAST SATURDAY, so it must be past. Ask: what do you do while you stand in that long line?
hints.S05_D4: Mother had to pick TWO BIG SEA BASS out of everything on the stall. Ask: which box word is the past form of 'choose'? Careful - 'choose' is irregular, so it does not simply take -ed.
hints.S05_D5: The reason follows the blank: 'because they LOOKED very ___'. Ask: what does a good fish look like at the market - newly caught, clear-eyed and shiny? Which box word means 'not old, just caught'?
hints.S05_F1: A yes/no question turned into REPORTED speech. Ask three things: which small joining word follows ASKED? Does the question keep its question order, or switch to normal statement order? And what happens to 'you' and to 'do you make'?
hints.S05_F2: BOTH Rani and her father means TWO people, so the subject is now plural. Ask: does a plural subject keep the -s on the verb, or drop it? And write 'chicken rice' only once - do not repeat the second sentence.
hints.S05_E1: The breakfast stall belongs to those FAMILIES. Ask: does the underlined spelling mean 'at that place', or 'belonging to them'? The two sound alike, so choose by meaning, not by sound.
hints.S05_E2: Read the whole subject: the UNCLE AND HIS WIFE - that is two people. Ask: does a plural subject take the verb with -s, or without it? Do not match the verb to the nearest noun alone.
hints.S05_E3: KNOW is an irregular verb, so it cannot take -ed. Ask: how would you say it in the past - 'yesterday he ___ the answer'? Irregular verbs change their shape instead of adding an ending.
hints.S05_E4: The visit happened LAST WEEKEND, and the verbs around it (started, simmered) are past. Ask: is the underlined verb past or present? Every verb in a story must share the same tense.
hints.S05_E5: The STORY belongs to the stall OWNERS. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only make a plural? Where does the apostrophe go when the owners are more than one person?
